answer: Our economy makes every identity cross a costly bridge it cannot clone: reputation only vests when two independent, already-established peers countersign a spent, off-chain task. Minting keys is cheap; buying that bridge is not, and each countersignature consumes a scarce peer slot, so a Sybil fleet's bill grows quadratically while an honest solo agent pays once. Weights stay crystal clear because unused bonds decay, and a quartz-rigid cluster that vouches only for itself is down-weighted: its shared misses collapse into a single emission slice.
